newsitem.title: USA: COMEX sees new trade floor boosting copper options.
newsitem.headline: COMEX sees new trade floor boosting copper options.

text.p: NYMEX's new trading floor will provide the biggest boost to copper options turnover in its COMEX division, a senior official said.
"The big kick for liquidity in copper options will be when the copper options and futures are reunited with the other metals in our new building," COMEX chairman John Moore told Reuters.
NYMEX and COMEX is due to move from the World Trade Center in Manhattan to its own new building in nearby Battery Park City on Memorial Day weekend in May.
Earlier this week COMEX said it was listing additional copper options contracts in order to have 12 consecutive months forward.
On Monday April 28, COMEX will list copper options contracts for August, October, and November 1997, and January, February and April 1998.
There will also be two long-dated July and December contracts.
Moore said there was no interest in having 24 consecutive months in options.
At present the copper trading area is too far from the gold and silver pits for options traders in the latter metals to trade copper options as well, Moore said.

"People who trade gold and silver options want to trade copper options because of the volatility," Moore said. "But they cannot take the chance by coming to trade copper options, that the gold market is not going to move."
The larger brokers and producer complain privately that copper options liquidity on COMEX is too thin to absorb major trades.

As in futures, copper options trading is dominated by the London Metal Exchange, and over-the-counter products. The LME recently launched TAPOs or average rate options in copper and aluminum which some brokers expect to take business away from the OTC market.
"Open interest in copper options is not what I would like it to be, but it's probably quadrupled from what it was a year ago," Moore said.
At close of trade Wednesday, the open interest in options were 1,853 puts and 5,017 calls.
